hypothesis: The official score is TP_w/(0.2*D + 0.8*N); the denominator does not contain TP_w. Therefore no single published dot pattern can be the best submission, and a score-calibrated consensus over the 128 published sibling rasters whose scores the owner typed - inverted through that algebra - recovers more truth credit per predicted dot than any individual file, and still does so after pruning to satisfy the 70% registry-overlap rule.
mechanism: Step 1: because alpha+beta = 1 and FP_w = D - TP_w, FN_w = N - TP_w, the official DTI of a binary prediction collapses to TP_w/(alpha*D + beta*N). Each published raster therefore pins its own truth credit, TP_i = s_i*(alpha*D_i + beta*N): one linear equation per file in the unknown field u(x) = P(x is within 300 m of a hidden truth pixel). Ridge regression in the file-by-file incidence space solves the 128x128 system in closed form with exact bit-popcount overlaps. Step 2: emit dots by descending u using the metric's own rule - a dot is worth adding iff q > alpha*DTI, about 0.06 at these scores - with a hard 2.0 px minimum separation, because two dots inside one 300 m kernel add 0.2 to D but at most 1.0 to TP_w. Step 3: greedily drop the lowest-u dots from whichever registry raster holds more than 65% of the file until every one of the 342 rasters is under the 70% limit.
mimic: Drainage, basin-margin lineaments and lidar-tile or survey-line striping. The consensus field inherits these wherever several published methods ran the same DEM-derived lineament detector, so part of its credit may be relief structure rather than faults. This is the named non-fault process that could inflate the estimate; it cannot be separated without the labels, which is why the estimate carries a +0.037 optimism correction.

evaluator_1.comparison: champion 0.2778 file = 0.064121 [0.056730, 0.071649]. Point estimate is higher (+13.6%) but the 95% intervals overlap, so this is NOT a significant win on this evaluator.
evaluator_1.concordance_note: Spearman rho = 0.8687 [0.6055, 0.9804] against owner-reported leaderboard scores over n = 21 files (evidence/proxy_leaderboard_concordance.json).

evaluator_2.comparison: champion 0.004515 [0.003816, 0.005262]. Higher, but this evaluator has Spearman rho = 0.143 [-0.378, 0.583] against the leaderboard (n = 21) and is NOT used as a decision metric.
evaluator_2.why_not_used: Organizers confirmed that known USGS/INGENIOUS fault pixels are masked out of scoring (forum thread 11516), so the ability to re-emit the visible catalogue is worthless on the leaderboard. HIDE-RECOVER measures exactly that ability; its anti-concordance is therefore structural, not noise.

holdout_dti.circularity_disclosure: SGMC-CAL scores recovery of USGS SGMC faults more than 300 m from the competition catalogue. A submission that simply re-emitted the SGMC raster would score near 1.0 on it, so the evaluator is circular in isolation. It is reported as corroboration only.

submission_note: CDTI-128 consensus 40,533 dots; est 0.394 (LOO sd 0.051); max registry overlap 64.0%
verdict_scope: A recommendation to spend one of the three weekly slots. Promotion to a real slot remains the owner's separate selector decision.
open_risks: Every calibration score is OWNER-REPORT typed by the owner, not an organizer receipt. One wrong typed value propagates into the fit.

The ridge field aggregates the owner's own published submissions. Correlated errors between those methods would inflate the estimate; the +0.037 optimism correction prices that, it does not eliminate it.
The estimate is an extrapolation: no published file exceeds 0.2778, so 0.394 lies outside the calibrated range.
SGMC-CAL, the only evaluator with measured positive concordance, shows a higher point estimate but overlapping intervals against the champion.

Uniqueness was measured against 342 of the 386 nine-site rasters and none of the wider ~2,900-file sibling pool; sparse dot rasters passed that wider pool in the 2026-10-29 sweep (max 42.43%), but it was not re-run here.
Phase 1 scores use a public subset; the private split and the GeoDAWN-wide final re-evaluation can differ.
